question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from United States of America?
option_2: Centrifugal form of federalism where the centre is stronger than the states
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fundamental Rights.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Fundamental Rights (मौलिक अधिकार) enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of the United States of America.

• Along with Fundamental Rights, features like judicial review, independence of the judiciary, and the office/impeachment of the President were also drawn from the USA.

• The USA is the birthplace of the concept of a written Bill of Rights, which inspired India's justiciable Fundamental Rights.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• There are six Fundamental Rights (Articles 14–32) at present after the Right to Property was removed by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

• Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning they are enforceable by the courts.

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

NOTE

• Centrifugal form of federalism where the centre is stronger than the states (Option 2): A federal structure with a strong centre, an idea borrowed from Canada, not the USA.

• Concept of Concurrent list (Option 3): The Concurrent List (Seventh Schedule) was borrowed from the Constitution of Australia.

• Single citizenship (Option 4): The concept of single citizenship for the whole of India was borrowed from the Constitution of the United Kingdom.

question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
option_1: To respect ideals of the constitution
solution_text:
The correct answer is Separation of judiciary from executive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Separation of judiciary from executive (कार्यपालिका से न्यायपालिका का पृथक्करण) is a Directive Principle of State Policy (Article 50), NOT a Fundamental Duty.

• Fundamental Duties are listed under Article 51A in Part IV-A of the Constitution.

• To respect the ideals of the Constitution, the National Flag and the National Anthem are all included in Article 51A(a).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• Originally 10 Fundamental Duties were added; an 11th (regarding education of children aged 6–14) was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002.

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and were borrowed from the former USSR (erstwhile Soviet Union).

NOTE

• To respect ideals of the constitution (Option 1): A genuine Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(a).

• To respect the National Flag (Option 2): A Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(a) to abide by and respect the National Flag.

• To respect the National Anthem (Option 3): A Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(a) to respect the National Anthem.

question: The 16th Islamic Summit of the OIC will be held in _____ in 2026.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Azerbaijan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 16th Islamic Summit of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (इस्लामिक सहयोग संगठन) is scheduled to be held in Baku, Azerbaijan in 2026.

• Azerbaijan will also assume the chairmanship of the OIC when it hosts the summit.

• The OIC is the second-largest inter-governmental organisation after the United Nations, with 57 member states.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The OIC was established in 1969 and is headquartered in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

• The 15th Islamic Summit was hosted by The Gambia in Banjul in 2024.

• India is not a member of the OIC, though it has a large Muslim population.

NOTE

• Gambia (Option 2): The Gambia hosted the previous 15th Islamic Summit at Banjul in 2024, not the 16th.

• Indonesia (Option 3): The world's most populous Muslim-majority country, but not the host of the 16th OIC summit.

• Morocco (Option 4): An OIC member in North Africa, but not the host of the 2026 summit.

question: Who among the following was named the goodwill ambassador for Earth Hour India 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is P V Sindhu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ace badminton player P V Sindhu (पी.वी. सिंधु) was named the goodwill ambassador for Earth Hour India 2024 by WWF-India.

• Earth Hour is a global movement by the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) encouraging people to switch off non-essential lights for one hour.

• Earth Hour is observed annually on the last Saturday of March to raise awareness about climate change and energy conservation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• P V Sindhu is a two-time Olympic medallist (silver at Rio 2016, bronze at Tokyo 2020) in badminton.

• She became the first Indian to win the BWF World Championship gold in 2019.

• Earth Hour was started by WWF in Sydney, Australia, in 2007.

NOTE

• Mithali Raj (Option 1): Former captain of the Indian women's cricket team, not the Earth Hour 2024 ambassador.

• Sakshi Malik (Option 3): Indian wrestler and Rio 2016 Olympic bronze medallist.

• Saina Nehwal (Option 4): Former badminton world No. 1 and London 2012 Olympic bronze medallist.

question: Har Gobind Khorana won the Nobel Prize in which field in 1968?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Medicine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Indian-American scientist Har Gobind Khorana won the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (चिकित्सा).

• He shared the prize with Marshall W. Nirenberg and Robert W. Holley for interpreting the genetic code and its function in protein synthesis.

• Khorana was born in Raipur (now in Pakistan) in 1922.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Khorana's work helped decode how the sequence of nucleotides in nucleic acids controls the synthesis of proteins.

• He later achieved the first chemical synthesis of an artificial gene.

• He was awarded India's Padma Vibhushan in 1969.

NOTE

• Chemistry (Option 2): Khorana was a chemist by training, but his 1968 Nobel was in Medicine, not Chemistry.

• Peace (Option 3): The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded for promoting peace; not related to Khorana.

• Literature (Option 4): The Nobel Prize in Literature is for outstanding literary work, unrelated to Khorana.

question: Who authored 'Bijak', a collection of devotional poems and teachings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kabir Das.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Bijak' is a collection of devotional poems, songs and teachings composed by the great Bhakti saint Kabir Das (कबीर दास).

• The Bijak is the sacred scripture of the Kabirpanth sect and comprises sections like Sakhi, Ramaini and Shabad.

• Kabir was a leading figure of the Nirguna Bhakti tradition, emphasising a formless God.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kabir was a disciple of Ramananda and is believed to have lived in the 15th century in Varanasi.

• His couplets (dohas) preach unity of God, opposing rituals, caste distinctions and religious orthodoxy.

• His verses are also included in the Sikh holy scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib.

NOTE

• Surdas (Option 1): Blind poet-saint of the Krishna Bhakti tradition, famous for 'Sur Sagar'.

• Raskhan (Option 2): A Muslim Krishna devotee-poet known for 'Prem Vatika' and 'Sujan Raskhan'.

• Mirabai (Option 4): Rajput princess and Krishna devotee, famous for her devotional bhajans.

question: In November 2024, Prime Minister Narendra Modi was honoured with the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Global Peace Award for Minority Upliftment in which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is United States of America.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2024, PM Narendra Modi was honoured with the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Global Peace Award for Minority Upliftment in Washington, USA (संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका).

• The award was presented in recognition of his efforts towards the upliftment and welfare of minorities in India.

• A new NGO for Indian-American minorities was also launched on the occasion in Washington.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The award is named after the American civil rights leader Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., who championed non-violence and racial equality.

• PM Modi is the recipient of numerous international honours, including the UAE's Order of Zayed and Russia's Order of St. Andrew.

• The award ceremony took place in Washington D.C., the capital of the USA.

NOTE

• France (Option 2): France conferred on Modi the Grand Cross of the Legion of Honour in 2023, not this award.

• United Kingom (Option 3): The UK did not present the Global Peace Award to PM Modi.

• Russia (Option 4): Russia honoured Modi with the Order of St. Andrew, a different award.

question: Purple Fests (Festival of Inclusion) has been organised in India since _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Purple Fest (समावेश का उत्सव / Festival of Inclusion) has been organised in India since 2023.

• The first Purple Fest was held in Panaji, Goa, in January 2023 to celebrate the abilities and inclusion of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan).

• It provides a platform showcasing accessibility, assistive technologies, employment and cultural participation of the differently abled.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The name 'Purple' is derived from the internationally recognised colour symbolising disability rights.

• The festival aligns with the aim of creating an inclusive society under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.

• Following its success in Goa, the concept has since been adopted at the national level.

NOTE

• 2020 (Option 2): The Purple Fest had not yet begun in 2020.

• 2021 (Option 3): No Purple Fest was organised in 2021; it started in 2023.

• 2022 (Option 4): The first edition was held in early 2023, not 2022.

question: _____ is a type of start which is essential for sprint races in sports.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Crouch Start.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Crouch Start (क्राउच स्टार्ट) is the type of start essential for sprint races in athletics.

• In the crouch start, the athlete crouches down with hands on the ground and feet placed against starting blocks for an explosive launch.

• It maximises acceleration at the beginning of short-distance races like the 100m, 200m and 400m.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• There are three common variations of the crouch start: the bunch (bullet) start, the medium start and the elongated start.

• Sprint start commands are 'On your marks', 'Set', and the firing of the gun.

• Starting blocks are mandatory in sprint events under World Athletics rules.

NOTE

• Vertical Start (Option 2): Not a recognised standard athletic sprint start technique.

• Jumping start (Option 3): Not a valid sprint start; jumping is used in field events like long/high jump.

• Standing Start (Option 4): Used in middle- and long-distance races, not sprints.

question: The Ramgarh Vishdhari Tiger Reserve is in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ramgarh Vishdhari Tiger Reserve is located in the Bundi district of Rajasthan (राजस्थान).

• It was notified as India's 52nd Tiger Reserve in 2022.

• It forms a corridor connecting Ranthambore Tiger Reserve and Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rajasthan is home to other tiger reserves such as Ranthambore, Sariska and Mukundra Hills.

• Project Tiger was launched in India in 1973 to protect the Bengal tiger.

• The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) is the statutory body overseeing tiger reserves.

NOTE

• Karnataka (Option 2): Home to tiger reserves like Bandipur and Nagarhole, but not Ramgarh Vishdhari.

• Odisha (Option 3): Has the Similipal and Satkosia Tiger Reserves, not Ramgarh Vishdhari.

• Jharkhand (Option 4): Has the Palamau Tiger Reserve, not Ramgarh Vishdhari.

question: Which of the following protected area of Odisha has been declared the 107th National Park of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Simlipal National Park.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Simlipal National Park (सिमलीपाल राष्ट्रीय उद्यान) in the Mayurbhanj district of Odisha has been declared the 107th National Park of India.

• Simlipal is well known for its population of Royal Bengal Tigers, including rare melanistic (black) tigers.

• It is also a Tiger Reserve, an Elephant Reserve and a part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Simlipal Biosphere Reserve was declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2009.

• India's first National Park was Hailey National Park (now Jim Corbett National Park), established in 1936.

• Odisha's other well-known protected areas include Bhitarkanika, Satkosia and Nandankanan.

NOTE

• Bhitarkanika National Park (Option 2): A mangrove ecosystem in Odisha famous for saltwater crocodiles, not the 107th National Park.

• Satkosia National Park (Option 3): Known for its gorge on the Mahanadi River and gharials.

• Nandankanan National Park (Option 4): Famous for its zoological park and white tigers near Bhubaneswar.

question: 47th HFI Junior Boy's National Handball Championship will be held in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 47th HFI Junior Boy's National Handball Championship is being held in New Delhi (नई दिल्ली), at Pitampura in the NCT of Delhi.

• It is organised by the Handball Federation of India (HFI).

• The championship brings together junior boys' handball teams from across various states of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Handball is a fast-paced team sport played between two teams of seven players each.

• The Handball Federation of India is the apex governing body for the sport in the country.

• Handball was first included in the Summer Olympics (as the modern indoor version) in 1972 (Munich).

NOTE

• Haryana (Option 2): A state strong in handball, but not the host of the 47th junior championship.

• Chandigarh (Option 3): A Union Territory, not the venue of this championship.

• Odisha (Option 4): Has hosted other handball events, but not the 47th Junior Boy's Championship.

question: The final round of the _____th Senior National Football Championship for Santosh Trophy began in December 2024.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 78.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The final round of the 78th Senior National Football Championship for the Santosh Trophy (संतोष ट्रॉफी) began on 14 December 2024.

• The Santosh Trophy is the premier state-level football championship in India.

• The 78th edition's final round was hosted in Hyderabad, Telangana.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Santosh Trophy was first held in 1941 and is named after Maharaja Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary of Santosh (in present-day Bangladesh).

• The tournament is organised by the All India Football Federation (AIFF).

• West Bengal is the most successful team in the history of the Santosh Trophy.

NOTE

• 70 (Option 1): Refers to an earlier edition held around 2016, not December 2024.

• 72 (Option 2): An earlier edition of the tournament, not the 2024 one.

• 74 (Option 3): An earlier edition; the December 2024 final round was the 78th.

question: The final round of 78th Senior National Football for Santosh Trophy was held in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hyderabad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The final round of the 78th Senior National Football Championship for the Santosh Trophy was held in Hyderabad (हैदराबाद), Telangana.

• Hyderabad hosted the Santosh Trophy final round after a gap of about 57 years.

• The final round began on 14 December 2024.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The matches were played at venues including the Gachibowli Athletic Stadium in Hyderabad.

• The Santosh Trophy is contested among the state associations and select government institutions.

• West Bengal remains the record-holder with the most Santosh Trophy titles.

NOTE

• Surat (Option 2): A city in Gujarat, not the host of the 78th Santosh Trophy final round.

• Mumbai (Option 3): The capital of Maharashtra, not the host city here.

• Kolkata (Option 4): A traditional football hub, but did not host the 78th final round.

question: Who is the author of the book 'Show Business', which parodies and satirizes formulaic Bollywood cinema?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shashi Tharoor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The book 'Show Business' was authored by Shashi Tharoor (शशि थरूर), a diplomat-turned-politician and writer.

• The novel is a satire on Bollywood and its formulaic commercial cinema.

• It was later adapted into the Hindi film 'Bollywood' (1994).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shashi Tharoor's other well-known works include 'The Great Indian Novel', 'An Era of Darkness' and 'Why I Am a Hindu'.

• He is a Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) and a former Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations.

• 'The Great Indian Novel' reimagines the Mahabharata in the context of the Indian independence movement.

NOTE

• Arundhati Roy (Option 1): Booker Prize-winning author of 'The God of Small Things'.

• Salman Rushdie (Option 2): Author of 'Midnight's Children' and 'The Satanic Verses'.

• Khushwant Singh (Option 3 wrong option): Author of 'Train to Pakistan' and 'The Company of Women'.

question:
Which of the following statement state the importance of the universal law of gravitation?
I. The motion of planets around the Sun
II. The tides due to the moon and the Sun
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The universal law of gravitation (सार्वभौमिक गुरुत्वाकर्षण नियम) explains both the motion of planets around the Sun and the tides due to the Moon and the Sun, so both statements are correct.

• The gravitational force of the Sun keeps the planets bound in their orbits.

• The gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun on the Earth's oceans causes the rise and fall of tides.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Newton's universal law of gravitation states that every body attracts every other body with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them (F = Gm1m2/r^2).

• The law also explains the motion of the Moon around the Earth and the falling of objects towards the ground.

• The value of the universal gravitational constant G is approximately 6.674 x 10^-11 N m^2/kg^2.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as the law also explains ocean tides (statement II).

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as the law also explains planetary motion (statement I).

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both are valid consequences of the law of gravitation.

question: What happens to solid carbon dioxide (dry ice) when the pressure is decreased to 1 atmosphere?
option_1: It sublimates directly into a gas.
option_4: It freezes further into a solid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It sublimates directly into a gas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Solid carbon dioxide (dry ice) undergoes sublimation (ऊर्ध्वपातन) — it changes directly from a solid to a gas — when the pressure is decreased to 1 atmosphere.

• At normal atmospheric pressure, CO2 cannot exist as a liquid, so it bypasses the liquid state entirely.

• Dry ice sublimates at about -78.5 degrees Celsius at 1 atmosphere.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Liquid CO2 can only exist at pressures above about 5.1 atmospheres (its triple point pressure).

• Dry ice is widely used for refrigeration, creating fog effects and flash-freezing.

• Sublimation is the direct transition of a substance from the solid to the gaseous phase.

NOTE

• It melts into a liquid (Option 2): Incorrect, as CO2 cannot form a liquid at 1 atmosphere pressure.

• It remains as a solid (Option 3): Incorrect, since dry ice readily sublimates in open air.

• It freezes further into a solid (Option 4): Incorrect; reducing pressure does not cause further freezing.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding the government budget?
I. Subsidies are an important policy instrument which aim at increasing welfare.
II. Defence expenditure, is committed expenditure in the sense that given the national security concerns, there exists little scope for drastic reduction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Regarding the government budget (सरकारी बजट), both statements are correct.

• Subsidies are indeed an important policy instrument aimed at increasing welfare (Statement I).

• Defence expenditure is a committed expenditure, as national security concerns leave little scope for drastic reduction (Statement II).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A government budget is an annual financial statement of estimated receipts and expenditure for a financial year (Article 112).

• Committed expenditure includes items like interest payments, salaries, pensions and defence, which cannot be easily reduced.

• Subsidies are a form of revenue expenditure and part of the welfare function of the government.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as Statement II about defence expenditure is also correct.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as Statement I about subsidies is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both statements are valid.

question: Shujauddaulah was the Nawab of which of the following region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Awadh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shuja-ud-Daulah was the Nawab of Awadh (अवध), ruling from 1754 to 1775.

• He fought against the British East India Company at the Battle of Buxar (1764), allied with Mir Qasim and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II.

• After defeat, he signed the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) with the British.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Awadh (Oudh) was a prosperous province with its capital at Faizabad and later Lucknow.

• The dynasty of the Nawabs of Awadh was founded by Saadat Khan (Burhan-ul-Mulk).

• Awadh was finally annexed by the British in 1856 under the Doctrine of Lapse-era policy of Lord Dalhousie (on grounds of misgovernance).

NOTE

• Amber (Option 1): A Rajput princely state near Jaipur, ruled by the Kachhwaha Rajputs, not a Nawabi.

• Mysore (Option 3): Ruled by Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, not Shuja-ud-Daulah.

• Hyderabad (Option 4): Ruled by the Nizams of the Asaf Jahi dynasty.

question:
Which of the following qualifications is required to contest the election of the President of India?
I. He or she must hold any office of profit under Central government.
II. He or she must qualify to become member of House of the People.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To contest the election for President of India (भारत के राष्ट्रपति), a person must be qualified for election as a member of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) — Statement II is correct.

• A candidate must NOT hold any office of profit under the Union or State governments — so Statement I is incorrect.

• Qualifications are laid down in Article 58 of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A Presidential candidate must be a citizen of India and have completed 35 years of age.

• The nomination must be subscribed by at least 50 electors as proposers and 50 as seconders.

• The President is elected by an electoral college through proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because holding an office of profit disqualifies a candidate, it is not a qualification.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, since Statement I is a disqualification, not a requirement.

• Neither I Nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because Statement II is a valid required qualification.

question: President shall from time to time summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, but _____ months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session.
solution_text:
The correct answer is six.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 85, a gap of not more than six months (छह मास) shall intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next session of Parliament.

• This effectively means Parliament must meet at least twice a year.

• The President summons and prorogues the sessions of Parliament.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 85 also empowers the President to prorogue the Houses and to dissolve the Lok Sabha.

• A 'session' is the period between the first sitting of a House and its prorogation.

• India usually has three parliamentary sessions annually: Budget, Monsoon and Winter.

NOTE

• twelve (Option 1): Incorrect; the constitutional maximum gap is six months, not twelve.

• three (Option 2): Incorrect; there is no three-month provision under Article 85.

• nine (Option 4): Incorrect; the specified interval is six months, not nine.

question: For how long a person can serve as a minister without being a member of either House of Parliament of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6 consecutive months.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A person can serve as a minister for a maximum of six consecutive months (निरंतर 6 मास) without being a member of either House of Parliament.

• Within these six months, the minister must get elected or nominated to either House, else he/she ceases to be a minister.

• This provision is contained in Article 75(5) of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A similar provision for State ministers exists under Article 164(4).

• The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)).

• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President, and other ministers are appointed on the PM's advice.

NOTE

• 3 consecutive months (Option 2): Incorrect; the constitutional limit is six months, not three.

• 12 consecutive months (Option 3): Incorrect; a minister cannot remain a non-member for a full year.

• 2 consecutive month (Option 4): Incorrect; the maximum permitted period is six months.

question: Rajya Sabha is required to return a Money Bill passed and transmitted by Lok Sabha within a period of _____ days from the date of its receipt.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14 days.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill (धन विधेयक) passed and transmitted by the Lok Sabha within 14 days from the date of its receipt.

• The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

• If the Rajya Sabha does not return the bill within 14 days, it is deemed to have been passed by both Houses.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A Money Bill is defined under Article 110 of the Constitution.

• A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and only on the recommendation of the President.

• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill, and the decision is final.

NOTE

• 7 days (Option 1): Incorrect; the return period for a Money Bill is 14 days.

• 1 month (Option 3): Incorrect; there is no one-month provision for returning a Money Bill.

• 20 days (Option 4): Incorrect; the constitutionally fixed period is 14 days.

question: What is the other name of the tissue fluid in human body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lymph.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lymph (लसीका) is another name for the tissue fluid in the human body.

• It is a colourless fluid formed when plasma, proteins and blood cells leak out of capillaries into the intercellular spaces.

• Lymph flows through the lymphatic system and helps in immunity and the transport of nutrients.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Lymph contains white blood cells, mainly lymphocytes, which fight infection.

• The lymphatic system also absorbs fats (as chyle) from the intestine via lacteals.

• Unlike blood, lymph lacks red blood cells and platelets.

NOTE

• Sweat (Option 1): A watery fluid secreted by sweat glands for thermoregulation, not tissue fluid.

• Urine (Option 2): The liquid waste excreted by the kidneys, not tissue fluid.

• Mucus (Option 4): A slimy secretion of mucous membranes for lubrication and protection.

question: Who was the Pallava king that built the 'seven rathas' at Mahabalipuram?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narasimhavarman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Seven Rathas' (सात रथ) / Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram were built by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla).

• Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) was named after his title 'Mamalla'.

• These monolithic rock-cut temples are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Narasimhavarman I defeated the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II and captured Vatapi (Badami), earning the title 'Vatapikonda'.

• The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.

• The Pallavas were pioneers of Dravidian temple architecture in South India.

NOTE

• Pulkeshin I (Option 1): An early Chalukya ruler of Vatapi (Badami), not a Pallava king.

• Rajendra I (Option 2): The Chola emperor famous for his naval expeditions, not a Pallava.

• Senguttuvan (Option 3): A Chera dynasty king associated with the Pattini (Kannagi) cult.
